rationale: Adding the control that distinguishes the applicability of the asserted growth defect. The claim has been that a quorum-less leader accumulates read requests without bound while CheckQuorum is false; the competing explanation is that the state is merely transient and would end quickly under the library's other liveness mechanism. The harness therefore now also runs the same retry pattern with CheckQuorum enabled and ticks the leader through an election timeout. A local run shows the window does close (after three ticks the node is StateFollower with pending=24 accumulated) but nothing is reclaimed: eight further read requests after the step-down do not grow the queue (pending_after=24, pending_unchanged=true, unconfirmed 0). That refines the claim in two ways: CheckQuorum bounds the growth window to roughly one election timeout, and the retention half of the defect is independent of CheckQuorum. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation; the interpretation is not revised until the receipt exists.

scope.description: Control for the growth claim: repeat the same-context ReadIndex retry pattern on a leader with CheckQuorum enabled, tick through an election timeout so the leader loses its quorum view, and record whether growth stops and whether the accumulated queue is reclaimed.
assumptions: Real raft instance built from newTestConfig with CheckQuorum set true over voters {1,2,3}, election timeout 3 ticks, ReadOnlySafe; no peer messages are delivered, so the quorum view is empty.
Retries are submitted in batches of eight between ticks (24 in total before the leader steps down), all with the same RequestCtx, which is the retry pattern the ReadIndex contract assigns to callers.
After the step-down eight more retries are submitted, so the harness also observes what a follower with no leader does with a read request.
excluded: Any claim that CheckQuorum is required or recommended for ReadOnlySafe; it is only used here as the competing liveness mechanism.
Any measurement of a network partition; the quorum view is emptied by delivering no messages.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceReadIndexGrowthWithCheckQuorum builds newTestConfig(1,3,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), sets CheckQuorum true, constructs the raft with newRaft, promotes it with becomeCandidate/becomeLeader and clears the outbound buffers. It emits a setup event (check_quorum, state, election timeout, voter count), then loops up to three ticks submitting eight same-context MsgReadIndex messages per tick while clearing outbound traffic, and emits a before event with the accumulated queue length, state and whether the window closed. It then submits eight more retries after the step-down and emits an after event with the queue length before and after, a boolean showing they are equal, the node state and the unconfirmed length.

comparisons.description: With CheckQuorum enabled the leader loses its quorum view within the election timeout, so the growth window does close on its own under that configuration.
Closing the window does not reclaim what was accumulated: further read requests after the step-down leave the queue at its previous length.

knowledge.assertion: the queued path accumulates one pending entry per retry and is not reclaimed by an authority transition
